name: Atlanta depot, Georgia Power PLL-18
notes: PORTABILITY TEST 2. Exists for the RATCHET. Georgia Power bills the greater of measured demand and 95% of the highest summer month -- against Nashville's 30%. R-5: typical commercial ratchets run 80-95% over 11-12 months and Nashville's 30%/12 is at the very bottom of the observed range, so calibrating only against NES understates ratchet severity by roughly 3x. One 30-minute excursion here sets a floor that survives a year, which is the single most expensive mistake a depot scheduler can make and the strongest argument for the forward view. Demand interval is 30-minute -- the Southeast regional trait, shared with NES and FPL.

tariff.notes: Demand $13.63/kW, 30-minute basis, and the 95% summer ratchet are from research answer R-5 (Georgia Power tariff PDFs). KNOWN LIMITATION, stated rather than approximated away: PLL-18 prices energy in DECLINING BLOCKS whose rate depends on hours-use of demand, so it has no clean $/kWh. The tariff object as built carries a flat energy list and CANNOT express that structure; the 0.055 $/kWh below is a placeholder, not a sourced rate. The demand side -- which is what a scheduler optimises against -- is faithful. Extending the object with hours-use blocks needs the block table, which R-5 does not carry; filed as a limitation, not silently rounded.
